vectors.name: mixed-case-email
vectors.note: salt lower-cases the address — this MUST derive the same key as `basic`, and a port that skips it fails login with a correct password

vectors.name: plus-tagged-email
vectors.note: the `+` tag is part of the address and is NOT stripped — a port that 'normalises' it derives a key for a different account

vectors.name: unicode-email-turkish-dotted-i
vectors.note: the salt is defined by JS `String.prototype.toLowerCase`, which is FULL case mapping: U+0130 becomes 'i' + U+0307 (two code points). Go's `strings.ToLower` yields a bare 'i' and derives a different salt — verified, not hypothetical

vectors.name: unicode-password
vectors.note: the password is UTF-8 encoded, including astral-plane code points — a port that treats it as Latin-1 or as UTF-16 units diverges

vectors.name: empty-password
vectors.note: PBKDF2 with a zero-length key; HMAC implementations sometimes special-case an empty key, and the UI layer sometimes refuses to send one

vectors.name: long-password
vectors.note: longer than HMAC-SHA256's 64-byte block, so the key is pre-hashed before use — the branch a short password never reaches
